study_metadata.title: AI-CyberGuard Stateful PortScan Detection Feasibility Study
study_metadata.author: Antigravity Agentic Assistant
study_metadata.objective: Investigate whether a separate stateful, multi-flow PortScan detector can complement the existing per-flow ML classifier without retraining or breaking baseline splits.

false_negatives_concentration.explanation: Target ports 139 and 445 were open on the victim host (192.168.10.50). Service version scans completed bidirectional TCP handshakes with graceful 2-way FIN teardown, rendering individual flow transport features indistinguishable from benign Windows file/print sharing traffic.

traffic_stream_chronological_audit.chronological_finding: 43.41% of rows in Friday-WorkingHours.csv are out of chronological order due to flow-generator export buffering. Evaluating rolling windows on unsorted CSV rows causes catastrophic false alarms due to timestamp thrashing. Offline stateful evaluation strictly requires chronological sorting by flow start timestamp.

attack_dynamics.scan_structure: Three discrete scanning phases separated by idle periods: (1) isolated preliminary probing (17:37 - 18:05), (2) moderate reconnaissance (18:55 - 19:15), and (3) massive automated sweep and service probing (19:50 - 20:23, over 158,000 flows).

stateful_detector_configurations_evaluat.description: Composite: Rolling 60s, >=20 distinct ports AND >=50% RST/failed flows
Composite: Rolling 300s, >=30 distinct ports AND >=40% RST/failed flows

false_negative_recovery_analysis.mechanism: The stateful detector triggered an alert on the attacker (172.16.0.1) at 19:51:45, within 43 seconds of the automated scanning sweep commencing. The 29 holdout false negatives occurred between 20:08:04 and 20:23:53 during late-stage service version inspection. Because the attacker source IP was already marked in an active ALERTING episode, every single late-stage probe is attributed to the ongoing port scan episode. This demonstrates that multi-flow aggregation completely eliminates the blind spot of per-flow classification on open ports without altering model weights.

false_positive_risk_analysis.client_workstations: Internal clients (192.168.10.3, 192.168.10.15, etc.) generated ZERO false alarms across all tested configurations. Benign browsing traffic peaked at 16 distinct destination ports in 60s and 20 distinct destination ports in 300s.
false_positive_risk_analysis.victim_server_reflection: The only false alarms in raw flow evaluation came from 192.168.10.50, which was the victim server responding to scanner probes on ephemeral ports. In an initiator-tracking architecture (such as stateful_initiator_v2), server response packets are correctly recognized as backward flows of inbound sessions rather than outbound scans, eliminating this false alarm source entirely.
false_positive_risk_analysis.infrastructure_services: 192.168.10.51 (domain controller / DNS) contacted 48 ports in 60s. Applying a threshold of >=50 ports (Config 3 or Config 4) completely silenced false alarms on this host.

engineering_recommendations.implementation_tier: Implement as a lightweight stateful aggregation filter within the ingestion pipeline (either in scripts/network-sensor.py or artifacts/api-server/src/routes/network.ts), running concurrently with the per-flow ML engine.
engineering_recommendations.recommended_configuration: Config 3 / Config 4: Rolling 300-second window tracking initiator IP, threshold of >=50 distinct destination ports (or >=30 distinct ports with >=40% RST/failed flow ratio). Cooldown period of 300 seconds of silence before closing the episode.
engineering_recommendations.coexistence_with_current_architecture: The stateful detector does not replace the ML model; it complements it: (1) ML model provides low-latency per-flow anomaly detection and high precision on closed-port sweeps; (2) Stateful detector aggregates flows across time windows, correlating open-port probes (which evade single-flow classifiers) into unified, high-confidence scan incidents with 99.998% alert compression.
engineering_recommendations.transition_guard_integration: This stateful detection logic maps directly into the existing stateful_initiator_v2 transition guard in Express, allowing seamless rollout without modifying production model weights.
